*   Accumulate reflection strength $R$ weighted by opacity and Gaussian weight [S1].

The claim states that the method accumulates reflection strength $R$ weighted by opacity and Gaussian weight. The evidence confirms that the method uses a 'reflection strength' parameter (scalar) associated with each Gaussian. It further explains that the rendering process involves a 'Gaussian splatting pass' where Gaussian properties (including reflection strength) are blended into screenspace maps using linear weights (opacity/Gaussian weights) as described in Equation 1 and the description of the two-pass model. Finally, the final color is composed as the sum of base and reflection colors weighted by this reflection strength. Thus, the accumulation involves the reflection strength, the Gaussian properties (which include opacity/weighting factors in the splatting process), and the Gaussian weights.

Unlike forward shading methods that compute reflection colors on individual Gaussians, this method separates Gaussian splatting from reflection shading, allowing pixel-precise normal maps to guide gradient propagation and environment map optimization [S1].

The claim states that the method separates Gaussian splatting from reflection shading, unlike forward shading methods that compute reflection on individual Gaussians. It further claims this allows pixel-precise normal maps to guide gradient propagation and environment map optimization. The evidence supports this in multiple places: 1) The notes explicitly state 'Differs from per-Gaussian shading... Deferred shading blends properties first, allowing gradients to flow between overlapping Gaussians' and 'Computes reflection on pixels instead of Gaussians'. 2) The notes mention 'The deferred shading model blends Gaussian properties into viewport-aligned textures... creating a gradient channel from color to blended normal to individual Gaussian normal'. 3) The notes state 'Environment map queries demand high precision on normal vectors... making normal estimation difficult' and the method uses 'per-pixel reflection gradients... to bridge the optimization process'. 4) The notes explicitly contrast with forward shading: 'Deferred shading produces better PSNR... than forward shading, where forward shading computes reflection colors on individual Gaussians'. All facts in the claim are present and supported by the evidence.
supported
